L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The most structurally relevant L1 context is the brigatinib/GSK1322322 scaffold, which shows absolute oral bioavailability of 46% (brigatinib) and 57-77% (GSK1322322 fasted/fed), all above the 20% threshold.
The lowest L1 bioavailability value among visible contexts is amsacrine at 32%, still above the 20% threshold; no visible L1 record affirmatively supports F<20%.

The query's N-methylpiperidine and 4-fluoro-3-chloroaniline substituents on a diaminopyrimidine-like fused core are structurally analogous to the high-F brigatinib/GSK1322322 context, supporting transfer of a high outcome.

evidence_gaps: No direct experimental bioavailability measurement for the query molecule.
L2 records are not yet available; only L1 current-gold records were considered.

Structural analogy to brigatinib/GSK1322322 is not exact because the query has a fused bicyclic diaminopyrimidine-like core rather than the monocyclic pyrimidine core, leaving absorption and metabolism differences uncertain.
